changesets.summary: Rate limit the API per client
changesets.details:
The new `monochange_app::rate_limit` module limits Leptos server functions and the REST endpoints under `/api` with [`governor`](https://docs.rs/governor) GCRA buckets. Requests with a valid session cookie count against the signed-in user's bucket (300 a minute, burst 100); every other request counts against its client address (60 a minute, burst 30), with IPv6 addresses grouped by their /64. Pages, `/pkg` assets, `/health`, and `/api/github/webhooks` are not limited.

`X-Forwarded-For` is read from the right and only when the peer is a loopback or private address, which is Caddy in the production deployment. The server now runs with `into_make_service_with_connect_info::<SocketAddr>()` so the middleware sees the peer address.

Limited responses carry `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` fields, and a `429 Too Many Requests` adds `Retry-After`. Server function rejections use the `ServerFnError` encoding (`ServerError|Too many requests. Try again in 12 seconds.`); REST rejections use the endpoints' `{"message": ...}` JSON body.

Override the limits with environment variables; a value that isn't a whole number above zero stops startup:

```bash
MONOCHANGE_RATE_LIMIT_ANONYMOUS_PER_MINUTE=60
MONOCHANGE_RATE_LIMIT_ANONYMOUS_BURST=30
MONOCHANGE_RATE_LIMIT_AUTHENTICATED_PER_MINUTE=300
MONOCHANGE_RATE_LIMIT_AUTHENTICATED_BURST=100
```

changesets.details:
monochange.dev now limits how quickly one client can call its API, so a single script can't slow the site down for everyone else. Normal browsing never comes close to the limit. Signed-in users get five times the allowance of anonymous visitors.

If you do hit the limit, the site tells you how many seconds to wait before trying again. Scripts that read the public task API get a `429 Too Many Requests` response with a `Retry-After` header, and every API response reports how many requests remain.

The new `components::repository_list` module renders them: `RepositoryFilters` (a GET search form that updates the URL in place after hydration), `RepositoryPager` (one list's pages), and `RepositoryPicker` (project-form checkboxes with a name filter that only hides rows, so hidden selections still submit). `RepoInfo` now derives `PartialEq` and `Eq`.

The dashboard no longer lists every connected repository at once. Each account folds open to its repositories, 20 to a page, in a list that scrolls inside the window. changesets.summary: Accept hosted release commits larger than 2 MiB

`POST /api/release-commits` now accepts request bodies up to 32 MiB (`monochange_app_api::RELEASE_COMMIT_BODY_LIMIT`). Before this change, the route used axum's 2 MiB default, so a grouped release that rewrote many changelogs was rejected with `400 Bad Request` (`length limit exceeded`) before it was authenticated. monochange's own release commits already send about 3 MiB of changelog content.

changesets.summary: Make hosted release commits match the files a local release commit stages
changesets.details:
`CommitRelease` with `commit_backend = "hosted"` now honors `stage_all = true`. Before this change, the hosted backend ignored the setting and sent only the files monochange tracks itself (changelogs, manifests, consumed changesets, and the release record), so files that earlier `Command` steps rewrote, such as `Cargo.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, generated schemas, or CLI snapshots, were missing from the bot's release commit.

With `stage_all = true`, the hosted request now also carries every path `git add --all` would stage: modified and staged tracked files, untracked files that `.gitignore` does not exclude, and deleted files (sent without content so the release commit removes them). Workflows that leave `stage_all` unset still send only the release-managed files.

The hosted backend now also filters release-managed files the way the local backend does before `git add`. It no longer sends `.monochange/local/release-manifest.json` or other ignored local artifacts, which previously landed on the release branch, and it only sends a missing path as a deletion when git tracks it.

```toml
[[cli.release.steps]]
type = "CommitRelease"
commit_backend = "hosted"
inputs = { stage_all = true }
```

changesets.summary: Split the CLI dispatcher and changelog validation into focused helpers
changesets.details:
`dispatch_cli_args` held every config-free fast path, configuration loading, clap error handling, `--jq` validation, and all subcommand arms in one function, and monostyle scored it at a cognitive complexity of 364, the largest complexity penalty in the repository. changesets.summary: Publish pnpm workspaces with pnpm under trusted publishing
changesets.details:
npm-registry packages in a pnpm workspace now always publish with `pnpm publish`, including when `publish.trusted_publishing` is enabled. Before this change, trusted publishing switched these packages to `npm publish`. npm does not understand the `workspace:` protocol, so any internal dependency declared as `workspace:*` or `workspace:^` was published verbatim and broke installs for consumers. pnpm rewrites those ranges to real versions when it packs.

pnpm 11 performs npm's OIDC trusted-publishing exchange natively, so trusted publishing from a pnpm workspace now requires pnpm 11.1.3 or later on the publishing runner:

```yaml
- uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
  with:
    version: 11
```

pnpm publish and placeholder commands also pass `--no-git-checks`. monochange validates the release commit itself, and release jobs usually run from a detached tag checkout with build outputs in the tree, which pnpm's branch and clean-tree checks would reject. npm, Yarn, and Bun workspaces keep publishing with the `npm` CLI.

sections.title: 🐛 Fixed
entries:
#### Make hosted release commits match the files a local release commit stages

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #803](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/803)

`CommitRelease` with `commit_backend = "hosted"` now honors `stage_all = true`. Before this change, the hosted backend ignored the setting and sent only the files monochange tracks itself (changelogs, manifests, consumed changesets, and the release record), so files that earlier `Command` steps rewrote, such as `Cargo.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, generated schemas, or CLI snapshots, were missing from the bot's release commit.

With `stage_all = true`, the hosted request now also carries every path `git add --all` would stage: modified and staged tracked files, untracked files that `.gitignore` does not exclude, and deleted files (sent without content so the release commit removes them). Workflows that leave `stage_all` unset still send only the release-managed files.

The hosted backend now also filters release-managed files the way the local backend does before `git add`. It no longer sends `.monochange/local/release-manifest.json` or other ignored local artifacts, which previously landed on the release branch, and it only sends a missing path as a deletion when git tracks it.

```toml
[[cli.release.steps]]
type = "CommitRelease"
commit_backend = "hosted"
inputs = { stage_all = true }
```

#### Publish pnpm workspaces with pnpm under trusted publishing

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #809](https://github.com/monochange/monochange/pull/809)

npm-registry packages in a pnpm workspace now always publish with `pnpm publish`, including when `publish.trusted_publishing` is enabled. Before this change, trusted publishing switched these packages to `npm publish`. npm does not understand the `workspace:` protocol, so any internal dependency declared as `workspace:*` or `workspace:^` was published verbatim and broke installs for consumers. pnpm rewrites those ranges to real versions when it packs.

pnpm 11 performs npm's OIDC trusted-publishing exchange natively, so trusted publishing from a pnpm workspace now requires pnpm 11.1.3 or later on the publishing runner:

```yaml
- uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
  with:
    version: 11
```

pnpm publish and placeholder commands also pass `--no-git-checks`. monochange validates the release commit itself, and release jobs usually run from a detached tag checkout with build outputs in the tree, which pnpm's branch and clean-tree checks would reject. npm, Yarn, and Bun workspaces keep publishing with the `npm` CLI.
